title: Day and Trial Passes: membership requirement, signup age, guardian consent, and identity checks
content:
This document covers the Day and Trial Passes product line: whether an active club membership is required to purchase a tier, the minimum age to purchase without guardian consent, whether guardian consent is required under that age, whether a government photo id is required to purchase, whether photo id must be shown at check-in, and whether an active corporate wellness sponsor is required.

## Per-tier basis

| Tier | Membership required to purchase | Minimum signup age (years) | Guardian consent required under minimum age | Photo id required to purchase | Photo id required at check-in | Corporate sponsor required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single Day Pass | No | 16 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Three-Day Trial Pass | No | 16 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Seven-Day Trial Pass | No | 16 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Weekly Visitor Pass | No | 16 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Monthly Trial Pass | No | 16 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Corporate Guest Pass | No | 16 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

None of the Day and Trial Passes tiers requires an active club membership to purchase; every tier is available as an ordinary walk-in purchase to a non-member, subject to its own other conditions. Every tier sets the minimum signup age at 16 years; a visitor purchasing under that age requires guardian consent. Every tier requires a government photo id to purchase and requires that photo id be shown again at check-in. Only the Corporate Guest Pass requires an active corporate wellness sponsor.
